assumed_deps: Python venv at scripts/../venv with celery.exe and python.exe in venv/Scripts
Redis (expected already running — script only hints to start it via WSL)
prechecks: None. Launches each component in a separate cmd window without verifying the venv, celery.exe, or redis exist before spawning.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: No validation. If venv\Scripts\celery.exe or python.exe are absent the spawned windows print errors but the .bat exits 0. Redis is never checked or started — only an echo hint is printed. Dependency failures surface only inside the child console windows.

assumed_deps: Python venv at scripts/../venv with celery.exe and python.exe
Redis (hinted to start via WSL; not started by this script)
prechecks: None. Launches Celery (worker -B) and the API in separate cmd windows with no existence checks on the venv or binaries.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: No validation. Missing venv\Scripts\celery.exe or python.exe produces errors in the child windows only; the .bat exits 0. Redis is not checked — the script only prints a redis-cli ping hint. Silent failure from the .bat's perspective.

assumed_deps: Running processes/window titles: empyrean-api, empyrean-celery-worker, empyrean-celery-beat
prechecks: None. Uses taskkill with /F /T and window-title filters; suppresses all output/error.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: Best-effort only: taskkill output is suppressed (>nul 2>nul). If no matching process exists the script still prints 'Stopped...' and exits 0. It never fails loudly — missing processes are silently ignored.

assumed_deps: python3, pip, alembic in remote venv
systemd and nginx on remote host
deploy/*.service unit files and deploy/.env.production.example template
prechecks: Checks only that SERVER_HOST is non-empty (exits 1 with message if missing). Otherwise relies on set -e to abort on any command failure; an ERR trap prints 'FAILED — see error output above'.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: If SERVER_HOST unset: exits 1 immediately with a clear message. If rsync/ssh/sudo/python3/alembic/systemd or the deploy/* files are missing, set -e aborts the script and the ERR trap prints a FAILED banner. Failures are loud and abort the deployment.

prechecks: None upfront. Each of the 4 phases is wrapped in try/except and reports OK/FAIL individually; check_postgresql probes the DB connection, check_migrations queries alembic_version.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: Each phase degrades gracefully: a missing import or unreachable DB is caught and printed as FAIL with the exception message. The script exits 1 if any phase failed (or 0 if all pass). Failures are reported clearly and loudly, but the script does not crash — it continues to run remaining checks.

prechecks: None upfront. DB connection is probed in a try/except; dependent checks 3–6 and 8 are SKIPPED if the DB is unreachable. Redis is probed with an explicit ping. Each check self-contains its error handling.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: Every check prints [OK], [FAIL], or [SKIP] with a detail string. DB-unreachable degrades dependent checks to [SKIP] (no hard failure on unstarted infra). A missing module/import causes [FAIL] with the exception text. Returns False and exits 1 if any check failed; exits 0 only when all pass.

If python is missing or verify.py raises, %ERRORLEVEL% is nonzero; the .bat pauses and exits with that code. Dependency problems are surfaced through verify.py's own FAIL output plus the paused console.

assumed_deps: Project modules: app, models, api, tasks, fuzzy, mqtt, celery_app
Redis/Celery not required for smoke (broker stubbed)
prechecks: None. _db_reachable() is a best-effort probe, not a requirement gate. Each phase is wrapped in try/except.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: Import errors within a phase are caught and reported as [FAIL] with the exception; the script continues to the next phase. A missing DB just causes [SKIP] for DB-dependent probes (never a crash). Exits 0 if all phases pass/skip, 1 if any phase [FAIL]. Failures are loud per-phase; missing infra does not abort the run.

assumed_deps: models package (User, Node, SystemSetting, get_sync_db, hash_password)
prechecks: Two explicit guards: refuses APP_ENV=production without --force (exits 3); requires SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD env var or exits 3. No upfront DB connectivity check — it opens a session and lets failures raise.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: Missing SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD → exits 3 with a clear message. Production env without --force → exits 3. Otherwise wraps seed() in try/except; any exception logs 'Seed failed: ...' and exits 1. DB/network failures surface as caught exceptions with explicit exit code 1.

assumed_deps: A running HTTP server at the target URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8000/health)
prechecks: None. Only argparse for URL/concurrency/requests args. Connects directly.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: If the target HTTP server is not running, asyncio open_connection raises ConnectionRefusedError or OSError; the script prints 'connection failed: {e}' to stderr and exits 1. No retry or probe beforehand. When the server is up, errors during the run are counted as 'errors' but the script still exits 0.

prechecks: Explicit: greps .env for a '^DATABASE_URL=' line; if absent, prints 'ERROR: DATABASE_URL not found in .env' and exits 1. No checks for psql/alembic/python presence.
fail_behavior_if_dep_missing: DATABASE_URL missing in .env → exits 1 with a clear message. Beyond that, set -euo pipefail aborts on any command failure (e.g. psql not installed, auth failed, alembic version mismatch) and the shell prints the failing command's non-zero exit. Failures are loud and abort the requested subcommand.
